A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenTract work, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. Their main sections and experiments can be matched reliably. v1 ends after the references; v2 additionally supplies supplementary Sections A–D.

before.justification: Sections 5.3–5.4 report original architecture comparisons, inference-step experiments, and HCP and TractoInferno evaluations, including Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments with revised baseline results and adds statistical findings and qualitative comparisons in supplementary Sections A and D.

M1.justification: The coefficient-wise VAEs, class-conditioned encoder, conditional Transformer, diffusion and flow-matching objectives, and selected DDIM inference procedure remain unchanged. The fODF wording and supplementary architectural specifications clarify the existing method rather than establish a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,042-subject HCP dataset and 28-subject TractoInferno test set, including the same original, noisy, and low-resolution-plus-noise coverage. The added qualitative examples examine subjects and bundles within existing HCP evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–5 evaluate the same comparators: tckglobal, iFOD2, SD Stream, DDTracking, and TractOracle. DDTracking was already evaluated in v1; its revised scores and newly disclosed inference parameters do not establish a different comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated location of Rician corruption from underlying/raw dMRI to the input fODF signal, with corresponding wording for the degraded-data evaluations. This materially revises the reported robustness protocol, although the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. The supplement also specifies 5,000 sampled streamlines for the new tractogram visualizations.

E4.justification: Supplementary Figures 6–9 add whole-tractogram comparisons, CC Oc and PYT L bundle examples across four subjects, and a degradation case exposing a GenTract failure. These extend the qualitative analysis beyond v1's SLFR example; the architecture and inference-step ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Supplementary Section A adds inferential testing across the central experiments: paired t-tests with one-sided bootstrapping, a p < 0.01 threshold, and significance findings for architecture selection and benchmark precision. v1 reports mean ± standard deviation but only refers to unavailable supplementary statistical details. No increase in repeated runs or seeds is established.

E6.justification: DDTracking's results are substantially revised throughout Tables 2–5. Its BS precision changes from 0.49 to 35.20, 0.44 to 5.41, 0.02 to 4.44, and 0.05 to 6.35, respectively. Table 2 bundle count changes from 9.30 to 49.69, altering baseline rankings; Table 4 TO-Net precision decreases from 12.75 to 8.42. GenTract's tabulated scores remain unchanged. Qualitative results are also replaced or added. The robustness revisions cannot be interpreted as established same-protocol gains.

T1.justification: The spherical-harmonic representation, diffusion objective, and flow-matching formulation in Equations 1–3 are retained. Neither version adds a theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the advantage over the strongest baseline from 2.1× over TractOracle to 1.8× over DDTracking, while retaining the 2.1× TractOracle comparison. Its degraded-data advantage changes from an order of magnitude to 3.5×. The introduction clarifies conditioning on fODFs rather than DWIs; the central generative-global-tractography contribution remains intact.

C2.justification: Supplementary Section D explicitly acknowledges failure to recover CC Oc under low-resolution-plus-noise conditions, adding a concrete boundary to the robustness claims. Section 6 adds uncertainty quantification through probabilistic sampling as future work. The broader limitations concerning proxy ground truth, restricted training bundles, and synthetic degradation were already present in v1.

D1.justification: v2 supplies previously omitted input and latent dimensions, 128-point streamline resampling, attention-head counts, batch size, epochs, learning-rate schedule, GPU-hour costs, and detailed baseline parameters and seeding procedures. It also explains constrained spherical deconvolution preprocessing and adds a training/inference code link. These substantially improve documentation without establishing that the underlying implementation changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Smith et al.'s anatomically constrained tractography reference for baseline preparation and removes Yang and Wang's noise-reduction reference previously used to support the corruption level. The related-work discussion and positioning against local and classical global tractography otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose are retained. Changes include localized terminology and preprocessing explanations, expansion of DDIM, revised comparison paragraphs, acknowledgements, and organization of the added supplement into Sections A–D.

P2.justification: Figures 6–9 add extensive comparison grids across subjects, bundles, and corruption conditions. Figure 4 replaces the DDTracking examples, Figure 3 is enlarged and repositioned, and the existing Figure 5 timing chart moves from the main text to the supplement. The principal table structures remain intact.

improvement.justification: The supplement fills important reproducibility gaps and documents a concrete failure case. The revised abstract and 2–3× speedup statement also better match the reported evidence. These gains are tempered by unexplained DDTracking score revisions and the changed corruption description; Section 5.4 still claims an order-of-magnitude advantage despite updated Table 4 supporting approximately 3.5×.
